What you are actually pricing

“App Store localization” searches mix two very different jobs:

  • Listing copy — app name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, What’s New, screenshot captions, App Preview scripts. You paste these into App Store Connect per locale.
  • In-app localization — every button, alert, and paywall string in Xcode or your cross-platform framework. Often thousands of strings across .strings / JSON / PO files.

The numbers below assume you need the first job — one zh-Hans storefront row — not a full app string dump. Confusing the two is how a $79 quote turns into a $4,000 surprise.

Freelancer pricing (Upwork, Fiverr, direct hire)

Marketplace translators usually bill one of three ways:

  • Per word — commonly cited at $0.08–$0.25 USD per source word for Simplified Chinese. A 400-word English description alone is $32–$100 before title, subtitle, keywords, promo text, and screenshot lines.
  • Flat “App Store package” — $150–$600+ for a bundled listing rewrite. Cheaper tiers often mean machine translation with light editing; higher tiers may include keyword research.
  • Hourly — $25–$80/hr for bilingual ASO-aware writers. A careful zh-Hans rewrite with keyword notes can run 3–6 hours ($75–$480) plus revision rounds.

Hidden costs: revision limits, timezone lag, unclear scope (did they pack the 100-character keyword field or just translate the description?), and no guarantee the copy fits Apple’s character limits until you paste into Connect.

ASO agency retainers

Boutique App Store optimization shops price for ongoing work, not a one-time locale add:

  • Monthly retainer — often $1,500–$5,000+ per month for keyword tracking, competitor monitoring, metadata experiments, and creative briefs across multiple markets.
  • One-off localization audit — $800–$3,000+ when bundled with en-US rework, Custom Product Pages, or paid-UA landing variants.
  • Enterprise localization vendors — TMS platforms (Phrase, Lokalise, Smartling) charge per seat and per word on top of translator fees — sensible at 20 locales and 10,000 strings, heavy for one indie app adding China.

Agencies earn their fee when you A/B test metadata weekly and run Apple Search Ads at scale. For a solo dev filling one zh-Hans row before launch, the retainer math rarely closes.
